title: Fit a mallet-finger splint onto a drooping fingertip: slide it on and bring the tip straight without bending it
instruction: Fit the splint fully onto the drooping tip of the trainer hand's index finger so that it holds the fingertip straight, without bending the fingertip further down or dragging the hand.
context: Mallet finger (a torn extensor tendon at the last finger joint, the fingertip drooping) is one of the commonest finger injuries; it is treated by keeping the fingertip straight in a splint, day and night, for 6 to 8 weeks, and the splint is refitted by the patient or a carer, where letting the fingertip bend even once restarts the healing. The fingertip cannot hold itself up, so the splint has to be slid onto it at its drooping angle and brought straight with it. In this task the droop is the first fitting of the splint, when the tip hangs down and the splint must be slid on and the tip straightened inside it; afterwards the splint is secured with tape and worn day and night (the tape is not part of the task).
setup: Metres; world x forward, y left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases; table top z = 0.7475. (1) Arm-elevation wedge, fixed: firm foam, vinyl covered, 250 mm wide (x 0.085 to 0.335), sloping 20 degrees up toward -y: 5 mm thick at its low end (y = 0.141), 66.6 mm at its high edge (y = -0.028), 180 mm along the slope. (2) Task-trainer adult right hand, free, palm down on the slope, fingers pointing up the slope (-y), the fingertips 50 mm past the high edge: adult median size, 86 mm across the knuckles, 26 mm thick palm, index finger 95 mm tip to knuckle (distal segment 18 mm wide x 15 mm thick, middle 19 x 16, proximal 21 x 18), fingers slightly spread, thumb beside the index, a 60 x 40 mm forearm stub at the wrist; silicone skin over a foam core, 0.290 kg plus 0.008 kg for the index fingertip. Its frame origin (0.270, -0.075, 0.8312) lies on the slope plane under the straight index fingertip's apex. The index finger's last joint (DIP, 26.6 mm from the fingertip) is a hinge: the fingertip droops 40 degrees toward the palm at rest; it moves freely from 5 degrees past straight to 70 degrees bent, with a passive spring of 0.02 N m/rad toward 37 degrees (0.49 N at the fingertip apex holds it straight). (3) Stack-type mallet-finger splint, free, 6 g, light-blue moulded plastic 1.5 mm thick, lying on the table hood up at (0.300, -0.200), its open end toward the hand (+y): 23.5 mm wide, 20 mm tall and 47.5 mm long overall; inside 20.5 mm wide and 17 mm tall; closed at the fingertip end; a hood over the first 31 mm (fingertip and DIP); beyond it the floor runs on 15 mm with 8.5 mm side walls, under the middle segment. Friction (static/dynamic): wedge 0.6/0.5, hand 0.5/0.4, splint 0.35/0.3. Real-world build: printable parts, spring specification and assembly for the hinged index finger and the splint are in trainer_build/ (BUILD.md, STL files, make_parts.py).
scoring: Measured on the splint and the hand. Sticky zero for the whole trial: the injured joint is ever bent more than 10 degrees past its starting droop (beyond 50 degrees), the hand is ever dragged more than 25 mm, lifted more than 15 mm or turned more than 15 degrees, or the splint falls below the table top. Otherwise credit counts only with both grippers at least 30 mm from the splint and the hand, and the splint and hand still (under 0.5 mm per 50 ms step) for 1 s: 0.3 if the splint is on the fingertip (the fingertip's apex no more than 20 mm from the closed end, the fingertip's axis within 5 mm of the splint's centre line, hood on the nail side within 30 degrees); 0.6 if also seated (apex within 4 mm of the closed end); 1.0 if also the joint is held straight (within 8 degrees of full extension) and the hand is on its mark (within 10 mm and 5 degrees). On another finger, upside down, held, still moving, or shallower than 20 mm: 0. Real-world check: the trainer's splint is clear PETG, so the fingertip apex and a mark 1.5 mm inside the closed end show through; ink dots mark the DIP axis on each side. Read the joint with a phone inclinometer or a protractor against the dots, the apex and seated marks by eye or photo, and the hand's position against its outline (trainer_build/BUILD.md).
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted demo takes 549 steps
reset_notes: Lay the hand back on its outline on the wedge, let the fingertip droop, and put the splint back at its mark hood up with the open end toward the hand. Check the resting droop (40 degrees, plus or minus 3, phone inclinometer) and the spring (0.49 N at the apex to hold the tip straight, kitchen scale) before each session; build and check steps are in trainer_build/BUILD.md.
fidelity: The trainer hand is rigid spheres, except the index fingertip: a hinged segment on a weak passive spring, standing in for a torn extensor tendon. The splint is rigid flat plates, not a rounded shell, with 1 mm of play around the fingertip. The splint is slid on and the tip straightened inside it; the securing tape is not modelled. A printable reference build is in trainer_build/ (untested as a print).
